series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 1/3] mm: swap: move LRU insertion out of the swap cache allocator
series_items.patch_summary: This patch moves the insertion of a new folio into the LRU (Least Recently Used) list out of the swap cache allocator function. The current implementation adds the folio to the LRU immediately, which prevents callers from acting on the folio before it becomes visible for reclaim. This change is necessary for two use cases: refault evaluation and zswap writeback dropbehind. By deferring the LRU insertion to the callers of __swap_cache_alloc_folio(), there is no functional change intended, but rather a preparatory step for future changes.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 2/3] mm: swap: refault on swap-in, not in the swap cache allocator
series_items.patch_summary: This patch moves the evaluation of page refaults from the swap cache allocator to the two callers that perform swap-in operations. This change prevents inflated working set statistics when zswap writeback continuously writes back compressed data. The patch also ensures that the shadow is handed back correctly in the swap cache allocation function, and fixes a potential issue with stale snapshots being used for refault evaluation.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 3/3] mm: zswap: preserve the workingset shadow across writeback
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue in the zswap compression algorithm where the workingset shadow is lost during writeback operations, leading to inaccurate anon refault/workingset accounting. To fix this, the patch preserves the workingset shadow within zswap by parking it in the zswap tree instead of overwriting it when allocating a new buffer folio. The parked shadow is then handled at the next opportunity, whether that's during swap-in, reclaim, or slot free operations.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series fixes a problem in the zswap writeback path where workingset refaults were being over-counted and eviction cookies were being lost, leading to inaccurate workingset detection. The patches preserve the shadow within zswap itself by parking the captured shadow in the zswap tree instead of erasing it when writing back to disk. This is done without introducing new swap-table or swap-slot state. As a result, refault evaluation is moved out of the swap-cache allocator and into the swap-in callers, preventing miscounted refaults. The patches were tested with a sysbench OLTP workload and showed significant reductions in workingset refaults, activations, and restores (-48%, -59%, and -53% respectively), while maintaining comparable writeback volume and unaffected throughput.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch downgrades the lock on the source inode during reflink operations from exclusive to shared, allowing other processes to access the file while a reflink is in progress. This improves performance by reducing stalls caused by concurrent clones and lseeks or dio reads on the src file. The patch also adds checks for direct IO writes that come in under EOF and ensures that the inode flag 'BTRFS_INODE_REFLINK_SRC' is visible to the dio writer. Additionally, it remains exclusive to dio reads through finishing the prep to prevent starving the clone on a stream of dio readers.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 1/5] SUNRPC: allow a service to opt out of rpcbind registration
series_items.patch_summary: This patch allows a service to opt out of rpcbind registration by introducing a new flag, sv_no_rpcbind, in the svc_serv structure. When this flag is set, the service will not be registered with rpcbind and the corresponding code paths are updated to honor this flag. This change does not affect any existing behavior as no caller has yet set this flag.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 2/5] NFSD: add a userspace-rpcbind flag to listener_set
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new 'userspace-rpcbind' flag to the listener_set interface, allowing callers to take over rpcbind registration from the kernel. The flag is echoed in the reply when accepted by the kernel, and the caller must not change ownership while a server exists. The patch also updates the netlink specification to include this new flag and its associated attributes.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 3/5] NFSD: honour the userspace-rpcbind flag in listener_set
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NFSD listener_set function to honour the userspace-rpcbind flag. When this flag is set, the kernel will not make an rpcbind call and instead sets sv_no_rpcbind on the service. This prevents synchronous rpcbind RPCs under nfsd_mutex and avoids issues with ownership changes. The legacy portlist add-fd interface also refuses to run against a service with this flag set. The patch affects several files in the NFSD codebase, including nfsctl.c, nfsd.h, and nfssvc.c.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 4/5] NFSD: report registerable programs in the listener_set reply
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NFSD (Network File System Daemon) to report registerable programs in the listener_set reply when a caller owns rpcbind. The reply includes the programs and versions that nfsd would have registered, as well as the listeners to register them for. This information is sent only when the request asked for it, preserving compatibility with older callers. The patch also removes unnecessary code and optimizes memory allocation for large listener sets.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 5/5] selftests/nfsd: exercise the userspace-rpcbind listener_set flag
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds self-tests to the NFS daemon (nfsd) that exercise its interaction with the userspace rpcbind service, specifically covering the listener_set flag and various scenarios related to registration, ownership, and teardown of listeners.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series allows userland to handle rpcbind registration for nfsd listeners, adding a new optional flag to the netlink downcall that tells the kernel to skip rpcbind registration. series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 01/11] mountd: factor out the per-path export attribute computation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the computation of per-path export attributes in the mountd service to make it more modular and reusable. The patch introduces a new function `export_attrs_build` that takes an export path and an export entry as input and returns a struct containing the computed export attributes. This function is used by both the upcall and downcall paths, making it easier to manage cross-mount subdirectories and re-exported filesystems. No functional changes are made, only code organization improvements.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 02/11] mountd: handle unmountable paths and junctions in the netlink downcall
series_items.patch_summary: This patch improves the handling of unmountable paths and junctions in the netlink downcall by nfsd_export(). It introduces a new function to check for junctions before denying exports, and splits the lookup_nonexport() function so that both downcalls can share the junction lookup. The patch also adds support for deferred requests, which are retried from cache_process() every RETRY_SEC seconds. This allows the kernel to keep the upcall pending in the meantime, improving performance and reliability.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 03/11] mountd: answer requests the kernel rejects on the netlink downcall
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mountd service to handle rejected requests from the kernel due to failed filehandle construction or other issues. When a request is rejected, it resubmits each entry individually and answers negative for any entries that are still refused by the kernel. This approach prevents pending requests from piling up and allows clients to recover from failures more efficiently.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 04/11] mountd: don't leak the parent export's fsid onto crossmnt submounts
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the mountd service where cross-mount submounts inherit their parent's fsid, leading to incorrect filehandles and ESTALE errors on clients. The patch uses export_attrs_build() to compute the flags, fsid, and uuid for each export, masking per-flavor secinfo flags as needed. It also honors the export's own e_ttl on positive entries and falls back to a negative entry when an export cannot be resolved.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 05/11] mountd: retry unresolvable fsid lookups on the netlink downcall
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mountd service to retry unresolvable file system ID (fsid) lookups on netlink downcalls. The fsid lookup is moved out of nfsd_handle_fh() and into a separate function, lookup_fsid(), which returns one of three possible values: FSID_LOOKUP_ANSWER (definitive), FSID_LOOKUP_RETRY (not resolvable yet), or FSID_LOOKUP_IGNORE (unusable). If the fsid lookup fails initially, it is added to a list of deferred netlink requests and retried on the same cadence as pipefs requests. This change helps prevent spurious ESTALE errors when the filesystem becomes available soon after the initial lookup failure.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 06/11] mountd: bound the junction path before copying it into e_path
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a potential heap corruption issue in the mountd service by bounding the junction path before copying it into e_path. The problem arises when a junction path exceeds NFS_MAXPATHLEN bytes, causing the strcpy function to write beyond the bounds of the fixed-size buffer. To prevent this, the patch checks the length of the junction path and rejects it if it's too long, returning NULL instead.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 07/11] mountd: give each worker its own netlink command socket
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a problem where multiple workers in the mountd process share the same netlink command socket, leading to incorrect sequence checks and potential data corruption. To fix this, each worker is given its own netlink command socket by reopening the inherited sockets in the child processes. This ensures that each worker has its own reply stream and prevents two workers from taking each other's acknowledgments or error messages during a round trip.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 08/11] mountd: retry export attributes that fail to resolve for a passing reason
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mountd service to retry export attributes that fail to resolve due to a passing reason, such as a temporary error or an inability to determine whether a path is exportable. The patch introduces a new return value of EAGAIN for cases where the decision cannot be made immediately, and keeps EINVAL for genuine errors. This change allows the mountd service to recover from temporary issues and improve its ability to handle re-exported NFS mounts.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 09/11] mountd: drop a deferred fsid lookup once it has been answered
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mountd service in the NFS-utils package to remove a deferred file system ID (fsid) lookup once it has been answered. The patch addresses an issue where an entry that resolves for the second time is still processed by nl_retry_expkey(), resulting in duplicate answers. To fix this, the patch introduces two new functions: delayed_expkey_matches() and delayed_expkey_remove(). The first function checks if a deferred fsid lookup matches a given request, while the second function removes any matching deferred lookup from the queue. The patch also updates the nl_expkey_singly() function to remove answered entries from the retry queue.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 10/11] mountd: bound the retry queues
series_items.patch_summary: This patch limits the size of three retry queues in the mountd service to prevent them from growing indefinitely. The queues are used when the server cannot immediately determine whether a client's filehandle is exportable, and they can be reached by clients through network requests. By capping these queues at MAX_DELAYED (1024 entries), the patch prevents excessive memory usage and latency caused by repeated deferrals. The cap only applies to new queue entries, allowing existing records to be re-queued without being dropped.

exportent.e_path, a fixed char[NFS_MAXPATHLEN+1].  Neither downcall

copy-on-write struct nl_sock carrying the same s_seq_next/s_seq_expect.
Only the notify sockets get nl_socket_disable_seq_check(); the command
sockets keep libnl's default sequence check, which each worker will
happily pass on the other's reply.

Two workers in a command/reply round trip can therefore take each other's
ack or NLMSG_ERROR.  cache_nl_set_reqs() then reports the wrong outcome
and the caller answers the wrong client and path - marking it exported,
retryable, or negatively cached.

fresh port id, so each worker gets its own reply stream.  The notify
sockets stay shared: they are receive-only, have the sequence check
disabled, and are nonblocking, so whichever worker gets there first takes
the notification.

review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the handling of statfs errors in export_attrs_build(), explaining that some errors, such as ETIMEDOUT or EIO, indicate that the path is not currently exportable but may be later, and therefore should return EAGAIN instead of EINVAL. review_comments.raw_body:
export_attrs_build() answers -1 both for a filesystem that can never be
exported and for one it could not measure this time:

 - nfsd_path_statfs() on a re-exported NFS mount can give ETIMEDOUT with
   "softerr", or EIO with plain "soft"
 - fsidnum_get_by_path() returns the same false whether fsidd is
   restarting, answered with nonsense, or has no fsid for the path

default_ttl.  An fsidd restart takes a working re-export offline until the
negative entry expires.

The netlink path turns EAGAIN into EXPORT_RETRY, and nfsd_export() leaves
the request for the next upcall, which is what both already do when
is_mountpoint() fails oddly.

is_mountpoint() callers use, plus two that are decidable even though it
does not name them:

 - 0: a chrooted worker thread ran the stat and its errno never reached

series_items.patch_summary: This patch introduces a new module parameter, cmdq_max_n_shift, which allows users to cap the command queue depth for SMMUv3 devices. The new parameter enables users to specify a custom log2 depth ceiling, ensuring that the queue never shrinks below one page.

review_comments.author: Breno Leitao
review_comments.summary: Expressed gratitude for fixing an issue he had previously encountered while investigating another SMMU problem. Did not provide any technical feedback or suggestions.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Wed, Sep 09, 2026 at 10:52:27AM +0100, Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) wrote:
> The command queue depth comes straight from the maximum the hardware
> advertises in IDR1, which reaches megabytes of coherent DMA per queue.
> A system with several SMMUv3 instances pays that per instance, and the
> Tegra241 CMDQV pays it again for every VCMDQ it preallocates.

Thanks. I've seen this issue while investigating another SMMU issue[1].
Thanks for fixing it.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260911-smmu_fix_aws-v1-0-75870bf9655b@debian.org/ [1]

> Queue depth only bounds how many commands may be in flight before a sync.
> A machine driving a handful of devices, or one with a tight memory budget,
> has no use for the maximum, and no way to say so.
> 
> Add cmdq_max_n_shift, a cap on the depth given as the log2 of the entry
> count, the form the hardware itself takes in the LOG2SIZE field of
> CMDQ_BASE. Decide the depth in arm_smmu_cmdq_max_n_shift(), which caps the
> IDR1 value for natural alignment and then applies the parameter, so the
> queue is allocated at the requested size. The Tegra241 CMDQV sizes its
> VCMDQs from IDR1 itself, so route that through the same helper.
> 
> Floor the request at one page worth of entries. Without the floor, a small
> request trips the CMDQ_BATCH_ENTRIES check in arm_smmu_device_hw_probe()
> and the SMMU fails to probe. The floor also costs nothing: coherent DMA is
> page granular, so a shallower queue occupies the same memory as one that
> fills the page.
> 
> Assisted-by: LLM
> Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>

series_items.patch_summary: This patch series addresses a memory allocation issue in the iommu/arm-smmu-v3 driver, specifically for kdump capture kernels. The problem arises when the SMMUv3 queues are allocated at their maximum hardware size, leading to out-of-memory conditions. review_comments.author: Yuanhe Shu
review_comments.summary: Tested the patch on an arm64 platform and confirmed it resolves the memory allocation issue. The patch was successfully applied to a kdump capture kernel, freeing up significant amounts of memory and allowing for successful vmcore creation.
review_comments.raw_body:
Tested-by: Yuanhe Shu <xiangzao@linux.alibaba.com>

We hit the same problem on our arm64 platform: the kdump capture kernel
runs out of memory because the SMMUv3 queues are still allocated at full
hardware size. We had started looking into it ourselves, then came across
this series, so we tested it on the affected hardware rather than prepare
a duplicate fix.

It resolves the problem for us - details below.

Test platform: an arm64 server, 128 cores, 2 NUMA nodes, 512 GiB RAM,
exposing 6 SMMUv3 instances. 64K-page kernel (PAGE_SHIFT=16) based on
Linux 7.0.14 with the series applied on top; crashkernel reservation is
512 MiB.

On this platform kdump FAILS without the patch, and the series fixes it.

Before - capture kernel WITHOUT the series:
  All 6 SMMUv3 instances still allocate the hardware-maximum queues:
    arm-smmu-v3 arm-smmu-v3.0.auto: allocated 524288 entries for cmdq
    arm-smmu-v3 arm-smmu-v3.0.auto: allocated 524288 entries for evtq
    arm-smmu-v3 arm-smmu-v3.0.auto: allocated 524288 entries for priq
    (... same for all 6 instances)
  That is 8 + 16 + 8 = 32 MiB per instance, 192 MiB total - 37.5% of the
  512 MiB reservation. The capture kernel OOMs before makedumpfile runs:
    swapper/0 invoked oom-killer: gfp_mask=0x2040cc0(GFP_KERNEL|...), order=0
    Out of memory and no killable processes...
    Rebooting in 10 seconds..
  => no vmcore is saved.

After - capture kernel WITH the series:
  All three queues are floored to one page per instance:
    arm-smmu-v3 arm-smmu-v3.0.auto: allocated 4096 entries for cmdq
    arm-smmu-v3 arm-smmu-v3.0.auto: allocated 2048 entries for evtq
    arm-smmu-v3 arm-smmu-v3.0.auto: allocated 4096 entries for priq
    (... same for all 6 instances)
  => ~1.1 MiB total (~191 MiB freed). All 6 instances re-probe cleanly
  (no -ENXIO, no allocation failure) and a 608 MB vmcore is saved.

Same machine, same 512 MiB reservation; the only difference is the v6
series, so this is a controlled before/after.

Thanks,
Yuanhe

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 01/12] mm/khugepaged: drop redundant mm_struct pin in madvise_collapse()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch removes unnecessary mm_struct pinning in the madvise_collapse() function, which is already holding a reference to the memory map through other means. The redundant mmgrab() and mmdrop() calls are dropped, simplifying the code and reducing potential issues with memory management.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 02/12] mm/khugepaged: count collapses where khugepaged makes them
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the khugepaged functionality to count collapses where it makes them, rather than relying on the caller to increment a shared counter. The daemon is able to keep its own counter without interference from the shared path. This change simplifies the code and improves maintainability.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 03/12] mm/khugepaged: rename mthp_present_ptes bitmap to eligible_ptes
series_items.patch_summary: This patch renames the bitmap 'mthp_present_ptes' to 'eligible_ptes' in the mm/khugepaged module. The name change reflects that a set bit in this bitmap indicates not only that a PTE is present, but also that it has passed additional checks such as uffd, lazyfree, anonymity, and sharing. The patch updates comments and code accordingly without introducing any functional changes.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 04/12] mm/collapse: add collapse.h for the collapse interface
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new header file, mm/collapse.h, to separate the interface and implementation of the collapse feature from khugepaged.c. The header file defines an enum for scan results and a struct for collapse control, as well as two constants that were previously defined in khugepaged.c. This separation is intended to draw a clear line between the user and engine sides of the collapse mechanism, improving maintainability and modularity.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 05/12] mm/collapse: state what a collapse may do in the policy
series_items.patch_summary: This patch introduces a new struct collapse_policy to store the policy decisions made by the caller before asking the kernel to collapse memory pages. The policy includes settings such as limits on empty, swapped-out or shared PTEs, whether to take strict rules for sub-PMD windows, and how hard to try for a destination folio. The patch removes the need for the kernel to look up who called it to make these decisions, instead allowing the caller to fill in the policy once per scan pass or call. This change simplifies the code and improves performance by reducing unnecessary checks.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 06/12] mm/collapse: drop the collapse_possible() wrapper
series_items.patch_summary: This patch removes a wrapper function called collapse_possible() that simply forwards to another function called collapse_possible_orders(). The three callers of collapse_possible() can directly test the mask returned by collapse_possible_orders(), eliminating the need for an extra function call. This change has no functional impact and is a minor optimization.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 07/12] mm/collapse: name the per-table scan reset for what it resets
series_items.patch_summary: This patch renames the function collapse_control_init_scan to collapse_scan_reset to better reflect its purpose of resetting scan accumulations before each PTE table scan. The rename is done to prepare for future changes where a control will have an init and release function, each run once per series of scans. No functional change is made.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 08/12] mm/collapse: separate scanning a PTE table from collapsing it
series_items.patch_summary: This patch separates the scanning of a PTE table from collapsing it into two distinct functions: collapse_scan_pmd() and collapse_run_pmd(). The scan function reads the table under mmap_lock, while the run function performs the actual collapse. This change improves code organization and reduces complexity by separating these two tasks. Additionally, this patch introduces changes to tracing and khugepaged behavior, including new tracing events and adjustments to how file tables are handled.

hog the lock.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 11/12] mm/collapse: declare the collapse interface in collapse.h
series_items.patch_summary: This patch declares the collapse interface in collapse.h, making it possible to use the collapse functionality from other kernel files. The interface includes four functions: collapse_control_init, collapse_scan_pmd, collapse_run_pmd, and collapse_control_release, which are called in a specific order with the mmap_lock held at different times. Additionally, two new functions are added: collapse_possible_orders and collapse_vma_revalidate. series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 12/12] mm/collapse: implement MADV_COLLAPSE in madvise.c
series_items.patch_summary: This patch moves the implementation of MADV_COLLAPSE from khugepaged.c to madvise.c, where it belongs among other madvise operations. This change simplifies the code and removes unnecessary dependencies between the daemon's file and the syscall implementation. The !CONFIG_TRANSPARENT_HUGEPAGE stub is also moved along with the rest of the code. The MADV_COLLAPSE operation remains a caller of the interface used by khugepaged, so its functionality does not change.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series separates the collapse engine from its callers in the Linux kernel's memory management code. The current implementation has the collapse engine and its callers intertwined, making it difficult to understand and maintain. This patch series draws a clear boundary between the two by introducing an interface for the collapse engine and moving the syscall to madvise.c. The engine is now split into four calls: initialization, policy setup, scanning under mmap_lock, and running without mmap_lock. This change improves modularity, readability, and maintainability of the code.

On 9/10/26 8:02 PM, Kiryl Shutsemau wrote:
> From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>
> 
> Tests scattered through the collapse path decide what a collapse is
> allowed to do by asking whether khugepaged started it.  Between them they
> settle:
> 
>   - which VMAs are eligible, and how hard to try for a folio;
>   - how many empty, swapped-out or shared PTEs a window may contain, and
>     whether a sub-PMD window is held to a stricter rule than a PMD;
>   - whether a range has to look used, and whether a MADV_FREE'd page is
>     left alone;
>   - whether the PMD is mapped as part of the request, and whether dirty
>     pages are worth writing back and retrying.
> 
> None of those is a fact about khugepaged.  Each is something the caller
> decided before asking, and the collapse code should not have to look up
> who called to find out.
> 
> Add struct collapse_policy for the caller to fill: khugepaged from its
> own settings, MADV_COLLAPSE from the fact that a user asked explicitly.
> Every test becomes a read of a field, and cc->is_khugepaged goes, having
> no reader left.
> 
> khugepaged fills the policy once per scan pass, MADV_COLLAPSE once per
> call.  That is the one change in behaviour.  The max_ptes_* limits and the
> defrag setting behind the allocation mask are sampled once per pass rather
> than on every table.  A table scanned early in a pass and one scanned late
> are then judged alike.
> 
> collapse_file() also drops a NULL check on the collapse_control.  It has
> one call site, reached only from collapse_single_pmd(), which dereferences
> cc unconditionally, so the check was already dead.
> 
> Assisted-by: LLM
> Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
> ---

Thanks. The logic is much clearer now.

On 9/10/26 8:02 PM, Kiryl Shutsemau wrote:
> From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>
> 
> A collapse is two jobs.  One reads a PTE table under mmap_lock and decides
> whether the range is worth collapsing.  The other allocates, isolates,
> copies and flushes, and wants the lock given up first.
> 
> collapse_single_pmd() did both, so the boundary between them was somewhere
> in the middle of a function.
> 
> Give each half its own function:
> 
>    - collapse_scan_pmd() scans one table and only reads.  The anonymous
>      scan that used to carry that name keeps its body as
>      collapse_scan_anon_pmd(), and collapse_scan_pmd() is now the entry
>      that picks the anonymous or the file side.
> 
>    - collapse_run_pmd() does the collapse the scan asked for.
>      SCAN_SUCCEED from the scan means there is something to run; anything
>      else is why there is not.
> 
> collapse_single_pmd() is now the two of them with the mmap_lock drop in
> between, so its callers see what they saw before.
> 
> What the scan found and the run needs travels in collapse_control.  For
> an anonymous table that is the orders and the referenced and swapped-out
> counts.  For a file it is the file itself, the offset in it, and whether
> the PMD folio is already in the page cache.
> 
> The file side moves with the anonymous one.  collapse_scan_file() used to
> run with mmap_lock already given up, and called collapse_file() itself
> when the page cache looked worth it.  It now runs under the lock like the
> anonymous scan and only judges; the run does the collapse.  A file
> collapse works on the page cache and never sees a VMA, so the scan takes
> the file reference while it still has one and the run gives it back.
> 
> That changes what a refused file table costs khugepaged.  Every file
> table it scanned used to end its pass over that mm, because the lock had
> been dropped to scan it; now only a table it goes on to collapse does.
> 
> Two things on the file side stop being rescanned.  When the page cache
> already holds the PMD folio, the scan says so and the run goes straight
> to retracting the PTE table.  A run that refuses dirty pages and may
> write them back retries collapse_file() alone.  The checks the scan makes
> ahead of it are ones collapse_file() repeats under the page cache lock.
> 
> Tracing changes with it.  mm_khugepaged_scan_pmd and
> mm_khugepaged_scan_file used to fire after the collapse, so for an
> accepted table their status field carried what the collapse made of it.
> They now fire before it and read SCAN_SUCCEED for an accepted table.  What
> the collapse then made of it is for mm_collapse_huge_page and
> mm_khugepaged_collapse_file to report.
> 
> Assisted-by: LLM
> Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
> ---
>   mm/collapse.h   |  16 ++++++
>   mm/khugepaged.c | 147 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++------------
>   2 files changed, 128 insertions(+), 35 deletions(-)
> 
> diff --git a/mm/collapse.h b/mm/collapse.h
> index 7044dc71c7c2..346859a2184f 100644
> --- a/mm/collapse.h
> +++ b/mm/collapse.h
> @@ -88,6 +88,22 @@ struct collapse_control {
>   
>   	/* Each bit marks a PTE the scan accepted as a collapse source */
>   	DECLARE_BITMAP(eligible_ptes, MAX_PTRS_PER_PTE);
> +
> +	/*
> +	 * What a scan found and the run after it needs.  Live only between the
> +	 * two, and read by nobody else.
> +	 *
> +	 * The file side takes a reference while it still has the VMA, since a
> +	 * file collapse works on the page cache and never sees one; the run is
> +	 * what gives it back.  A scan that found the PMD folio already in the
> +	 * cache leaves only the PTE table to retract.
> +	 */
> +	unsigned long scan_orders;
> +	int scan_referenced;
> +	int scan_unmapped;
> +	struct file *scan_file;
> +	pgoff_t scan_pgoff;
> +	bool scan_retract_only;
>   };

[snip]

> +
> +static enum scan_result collapse_scan_pmd(struct vm_area_struct *vma,
> +		unsigned long addr, struct collapse_control *cc)
>   {
> -	struct mm_struct *mm = vma->vm_mm;
> -	bool triggered_wb = false;
>   	enum scan_result result;
> -	struct file *file;
>   	pgoff_t pgoff;
>   
> -	mmap_assert_locked(mm);
> +	mmap_assert_locked(vma->vm_mm);
> +	/* Whatever the last scan found has to have been run by now */
> +	if (WARN_ON_ONCE(cc->scan_file)) {
> +		fput(cc->scan_file);
> +		cc->scan_file = NULL;
> +	}
>   
>   	if (vma_is_anonymous(vma))
> -		return collapse_scan_pmd(mm, vma, addr, lock_dropped, cc);
> +		return collapse_scan_anon_pmd(vma, addr, cc);
>   
> -	file = get_file(vma->vm_file);
>   	pgoff = linear_page_index(vma, addr);
> +	result = collapse_scan_file(vma->vm_mm, addr, vma->vm_file, pgoff, cc);
> +	switch (result) {
> +	case SCAN_SUCCEED:
> +		cc->scan_retract_only = false;
> +		break;
> +	case SCAN_PTE_MAPPED_HUGEPAGE:
> +		/*
> +		 * The page cache already holds the PMD folio; what is left is
> +		 * to retract the PTE table, which is the run's job.
> +		 */
> +		cc->scan_retract_only = true;
> +		result = SCAN_SUCCEED;
> +		break;
> +	default:
> +		return result;
> +	}
>   
> -	mmap_read_unlock(mm);
> -	*lock_dropped = true;
> +	/*
> +	 * A file collapse works on the page cache and never sees a VMA, so take
> +	 * what it needs from this one while it is still here.
> +	 */
> +	cc->scan_file = get_file(vma->vm_file);
> +	cc->scan_pgoff = pgoff;
> +	return result;
> +}
> +
> +static enum scan_result collapse_run_pmd(struct mm_struct *mm,
> +		unsigned long addr, struct collapse_control *cc)
> +{
> +	struct file *file = cc->scan_file;
> +	bool triggered_wb = false;
> +	enum scan_result result;
> +	pgoff_t pgoff;
> +
> +	if (!file)
> +		return mthp_collapse(mm, addr, cc->scan_referenced,
> +				     cc->scan_unmapped, cc, cc->scan_orders);

You already record scan_referenced, scan_unmapped, and scan_orders in 
'cc'. It looks like simply passing 'cc' as a parameter should be enough.

> From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>
> 
> The scan asked collapse_possible_orders() for every PTE table, for an
> answer that is a property of the VMA.  Both callers walk a VMA a table at
